Here are four multiple choice questions about 20th century art history:

Question 1: Who is the artist associated with the painting "No. 61 (Rust and Blue)"?

A) Mark Rothko
B) Jackson Pollock
C) Willem de Kooning
D) Barnett Newman
E) Franz Kline

Question 2: Which art movement, emerging in the 1910s, emphasized the use of industrial materials and techniques to create a new kind of art?

A) Fauvism
B) Cubism
C) Futurism
D) Constructivism
E) Surrealism

Question 3: The artist Marcel Duchamp is often credited with creating the first conceptual art piece, "Fountain" (1917), which challenged traditional notions of art by presenting a urinal as a work of art. What was the significance of this piece in the development of modern art?

A) It marked the beginning of abstract expressionism
B) It introduced the concept of appropriation art
C) It questioned the definition of art and its relationship to society
D) It showcased Duchamp's skill as a sculptor
E) It was a response to the rise of modernism

Question 4: The art historian and critic Clement Greenberg was a key figure in the development of modern art criticism, and his essay "Avant-Garde and Kitsch" (1939) is considered a seminal work in the field of art criticism. In this essay, Greenberg argued that the avant-garde movement of the early 20th century was characterized by a rejection of traditional artistic forms and a focus on the creation of a new kind of art that was more authentic and expressive. What was the central argument of Greenberg's essay, and how did it reflect the broader cultural and artistic trends of the time?

A) The avant-garde movement was a response to the commercialization of art
B) The avant-garde movement was a rejection of traditional artistic forms and a focus on the creation of a new kind of art
C) The avant-garde movement was a celebration of the beauty of modern technology
D) The avant-garde movement was a response to the rise of fascist ideology
E) The avant-garde movement was a rejection of the role of the artist as a social critic
